entities.name: O Fortuna
entities.label: Text
entities.summary:
O Fortuna, a Latin poem created around 1300, is a medieval masterpiece that encapsulates the human experience of fate and mortality. Written in the style of the Roman poet Virgil, O Fortuna is a lamentation on the transience of life and the inevitability of destiny. Its 13 stanzas and over 700 lines weave a complex tapestry of mythological and historical references, from the rise and fall of empires to the fleeting nature of human passion. The poem's themes of impermanence and the cyclical nature of time have resonated with readers for centuries, making O Fortuna a cornerstone of medieval literature and a testament to the power of poetry to capture the human condition. With its rich imagery and soaring language, O Fortuna is a work that continues to captivate audiences today, inspiring new interpretations and analyses of its significance in the arc of world history.

The poem's creation and dissemination are shrouded in mystery, with some attributing it to the French poet Guillaume de Machaut, while others claim it was written by the German poet Wolfram von Eschenbach. Regardless of its authorship, O Fortuna's impact on Western literature is undeniable, influencing countless poets and writers, from Dante Alighieri to T.S. Eliot. Its influence extends beyond the realm of literature, too, with O Fortuna becoming a cultural touchstone, referenced in everything from music to film to advertising. The poem's legacy is a testament to the enduring power of art to transcend time and speak to the human experience.
